## Functions

### `brapiBaseOf`

The BrAPI base of an endpoint URL: everything up to and including the
`/brapi/v<N>` segment (`/proxy/brapi/v2/allelematrix-search?x=1` →
`/proxy/brapi/v2`). When the path has no such segment, the
`/allelematrix-search…` tail is stripped as the prototype did
(`main.tsx:731-732`), and only when that tail is absent too is the last
path segment dropped. Pure string work: relative and absolute URLs both
work; the query string is discarded.

```ts
function brapiBaseOf(matrixUrl: string): string;
```

### `brapiPages`

Iterate a paged BrAPI list endpoint: GET `url` with `pageSize` and
`page=0,1,…`, yielding each page's `result.data` with its pagination
block, and stopping once `currentPage >= totalPages - 1`, after `maxPages`
pages, or when a page carries no pagination block (treated as the only
page). Paging is new in tbrowse-core: the playground prototype issued a
single `pageSize=10000` request (`main.tsx:733-734`). Missing counts default to
the page index / 1 / `data.length`.

```ts
function brapiPages<T>(url: string, opts?: BrapiFetchOptions & {
    pageSize?: number;
    maxPages?: number;
}): AsyncGenerator<BrapiPage<T>>;
```

### `brapiVariantsUrlFrom`

The `/variants` URL for the window an `/allelematrix-search` URL covers:
the path's `/allelematrix-search…` tail becomes `/variants` (or
`/variants` is appended to `brapiBaseOf(matrixUrl)` when that tail is
absent), and EVERY query parameter is kept except `tree` — the region,
sample and allele-frequency filters must match the matrix exactly
(`main.tsx:681-684`).

```ts
function brapiVariantsUrlFrom(matrixUrl: string): string;
```

### `createLoader`

Creates a `Loader` for a source. `start(ctx)` aborts any previous
generation, loads the root, then runs every enabled eager slot
concurrently; `load(slotId)` runs a lazy slot or retries an errored one.
The snapshot's `data` is always `root.data` + `toHostData()` of every
ready slot merged in slot declaration order, whatever order the slots
settled in. `getSnapshot()` returns the same reference until a field
actually changes; `subscribe` returns an unsubscribe. `abort()` cancels
in-flight work (in-flight slots become `'error'` / `'aborted'`) and
`dispose()` drops every listener first, then aborts, so nothing is
notified after disposal.

```ts
function createLoader<Ctx, M>(source: TreeDataSource<Ctx, M>, options?: LoaderOptions): Loader<Ctx, M>;
```

### `defineSlot`

Identity helper that pins a slot's `T`, `Ctx` and `M` so the `run` /
`toHostData` / `failWhen` members are type-checked against each other
without the caller writing the generics twice.

```ts
function defineSlot<T, Ctx, M>(slot: DataSlot<T, Ctx, M>): DataSlot<T, Ctx, M>;
```

### `ensemblGeneTreeUrl`

URL of the gene-tree-by-member endpoint for `geneId`, switching the route
on the host's release (see `EnsemblMirror.route`).

```ts
function ensemblGeneTreeUrl(geneId: string, opts?: EnsemblGeneTreeUrlOptions): string;
```

### `expandCigar`

Expand a Gramene CIGAR string against an unaligned protein sequence.

The encoding here only uses `M` (consume <run> residues from the unaligned
sequence) and `D` (emit <run> gap characters). E.g. `expandCigar("MKLV", "2M1D2M")`
→ `"MK-LV"`. Run length defaults to 1 when omitted (e.g. `"M1DM"`).

Public so hosts that fetch Gramene leaf documents themselves can
reconstruct aligned rows without going through `fromGrameneGenetree`.

Origin: moved verbatim from `tbrowse/src/adapters/gramene.ts:235`.

```ts
function expandCigar(sequence: string, cigar: string): string;
```

### `extendSource`

Derives a new source from `source`: the same `loadRoot`, `id` from the
patch (default: the original id), and `slots` = the original slots minus
the `without` ids, with each given slot either replacing the existing
slot of the same id IN PLACE (keeping declaration order, and hence the
host-data merge order) or appended. `Ctx2 extends Ctx` lets the added
slots read extra context fields the original source never sees.

```ts
function extendSource<Ctx, M, Ctx2 extends Ctx = Ctx>(source: TreeDataSource<Ctx, M>, patch: {
    id?: string;
    slots?: readonly DataSlot<any, Ctx2, M>[];
    without?: readonly string[];
}): TreeDataSource<Ctx2, M>;
```

### `facetPairsToCounts`

Turn a Solr flat facet array (`[value, count, value, count, …]`) into
`{ [String(value)]: count }`. Missing or non-numeric counts become 0
(the origin's unary `+` would yield `NaN`). Origin:
gramene-search `taxTree/countsZone.js:24-28`.

```ts
function facetPairsToCounts(facet: ReadonlyArray<string | number> | undefined): Record<string, number>;
```

### `fetchBrapiAlleleMatrix`

GET an `/allelematrix-search` URL and normalise it with `fromBrAPIAlleleMatrix`.

```ts
function fetchBrapiAlleleMatrix(url: string, opts?: BrapiFetchOptions & {
    regionLabel?: string;
}): Promise<FromBrAPIAlleleMatrixResult>;
```

### `fetchBrapiGermplasm`

Page through `{base}/germplasm` (`pageSize` default 1000) and return the
records for `ids` only, keyed as `fromBrAPIGermplasm` keys them
(germplasmDbId and germplasmName), so the result joins the tree's leaf
`geneId`s directly. Servers often expose far more germplasm than ended
up in the matrix, hence the filter (`main.tsx:750-757`).

```ts
function fetchBrapiGermplasm(base: string, ids: readonly string[], opts?: BrapiFetchOptions & {
    pageSize?: number;
    maxPages?: number;
}): Promise<Record<GeneId, Germplasm>>;
```

### `fetchBrapiVariants`

GET a `/variants` URL (see `brapiVariantsUrlFrom`) and convert it with `fromBrAPIVariants`.

```ts
function fetchBrapiVariants(variantsUrl: string, opts?: BrapiFetchOptions & {
    reference?: string;
}): Promise<VariantSite[]>;
```

### `fetchBrapiVariantSetTree`

GET `{base}/variantsets/{id}/tree` — gramene-g2p's precomputed,
dataset-wide sample tree (`{ newick, leafOrder, samples, variants,
method, metric }`, optionally wrapped in `result`). Resolves null on a
404 (no build-tree run for that variant set); other HTTP errors throw.

```ts
function fetchBrapiVariantSetTree(base: string, variantSetDbId: string, opts?: BrapiFetchOptions): Promise<BrapiVariantSetTree | null>;
```

### `fetchEnsemblGeneTree`

GET the gene tree that contains `geneId` (via {@link ensemblGeneTreeUrl},
so the route follows the host's release) and convert it with
`fromEnsemblGeneTree`. A 404 is reported as "no gene tree for <gene>"
naming the host and release, because on Ensembl it is almost always a
route-shape mismatch rather than a missing gene; every other non-2xx
status surfaces as `HTTP <status> from <host>`. Origin: the playground's
`loadEnsembl`, `examples/playground/main.tsx:345-380`.

```ts
function fetchEnsemblGeneTree(geneId: string, opts?: FetchEnsemblGeneTreeOptions): Promise<FromEnsemblResult>;
```

### `fetchEnsemblOverlap`

Fan out to `/overlap/id/{gene}?feature=transcript;feature=exon;feature=cds;
feature=regulatory;feature=motif` for every gene id and split each
response into a `GeneStructure` (`fromEnsemblGeneStructure`) and
`GenomeFeature[]` (`fromEnsemblGenomeFeatures`). A gene whose request
fails, or whose response holds no gene model, lands in
`geneStructureErrors` with a message; the rest of the tree still gets
its data. Genes without regulatory/motif hits are simply absent from
`genomeFeatures`. Origin: the playground's `loadEnsemblOverlap`,
`examples/playground/main.tsx:480-545`.

```ts
function fetchEnsemblOverlap(geneIds: readonly GeneId[], opts?: FetchEnsemblOverlapOptions): Promise<EnsemblOverlapResult>;
```

### `fetchEnsemblProteinDomains`

Fan out to `/overlap/translation/{ENSP}?feature=protein_feature` for
every gene in `proteinIdByGeneId` (as `fromEnsemblGeneTree` reports it)
and convert each response with `fromEnsemblProteinFeatures`, keeping
only the `sources` given (Pfam + Smart by default). Per-gene failures
are recorded in `errors` rather than aborting the batch; the caller
decides whether an all-failed result is an error. Origin: the
playground's `loadEnsemblDomains`, `examples/playground/main.tsx:390-465`.

```ts
function fetchEnsemblProteinDomains(proteinIdByGeneId: Record<GeneId, string>, opts?: FetchEnsemblProteinDomainsOptions): Promise<FanOutResult<ProteinDomain[]>>;
```

### `fetchGrameneExprAttrDocs`

Fetch the expression-attribute docs (`id` + every `expr_*__attr_*`
field) for the genes of one tree in a single query: `q=*:*`,
`fq=gene_tree:<treeId>`, `fq=capabilities:expression_attributes`,
`fl=id,expr_*__attr_*`, `rows=10000`. Scoping by the capability means
only genes that actually carry the data come back; the glob `fl` lets
the columns be discovered from the data. `opts.treeField` replaces
`gene_tree` for a clade tree set. Origin: `Homology.js:293-331`.

```ts
function fetchGrameneExprAttrDocs(base: string, treeId: string, opts?: FetchGrameneExprAttrDocsOptions): Promise<Array<Record<string, unknown>>>;
```

### `fetchGrameneGene`

GET `{base}/genes?idList=<geneId>` and convert with `fromGrameneGene`,
which yields the gene's tree id (or `null` when it has none). Origin:
`main.tsx:655-663`.

```ts
function fetchGrameneGene(base: string, geneId: string, opts?: GrameneFetchOptions): Promise<FromGrameneGeneResult>;
```

### `fetchGrameneGeneStructures`

Fetch `gene_structure` (+ `location`, `name`, `canonical_transcript`)
for every gene id in chunks — `GET {base}/genes?idList=<ids>&rows=-1
&fl=…` — so the URL stays under proxy limits, and convert each chunk
with `fromGrameneGeneStructures`. Always sends `rows=-1`. A failing
chunk records its message under each of its ids in `errors`; genes
whose docs carry no `gene_structure` are simply absent from `results`.
Origin: `main.tsx:608-636` (chunk 200, narrow `fl`) and
`Homology.js:248-290` (chunk 50, no `fl`).

```ts
function fetchGrameneGeneStructures(base: string, geneIds: readonly GeneId[], opts?: FetchGrameneGeneStructuresOptions): Promise<FanOutResult<GeneStructure>>;
```

### `fetchGrameneGenetree`

GET `{base}/genetrees?idList=<treeId>` and convert the response array
with `fromGrameneGenetree` (tree, taxonomy, MSA, per-leaf domains and
exon junctions). Origin: `main.tsx:666-672`.

```ts
function fetchGrameneGenetree(base: string, treeId: string, opts?: GrameneFetchOptions & FromGrameneGenetreeOptions): Promise<FromGrameneGenetreeResult>;
```

### `fetchGrameneNeighborhood`

GET `{base}/search` with {@link grameneNeighborhoodQuery} and convert
with `fromGrameneNeighborhood` into per-gene ±10 neighbourhoods. One
request answers for the whole tree. Origin: `main.tsx:574-600`,
`Homology.js:217-247`.

```ts
function fetchGrameneNeighborhood(base: string, treeId: string, opts?: GrameneTreeQueryOptions): Promise<Record<GeneId, Neighborhood>>;
```

### `fetchGrameneSearchDocs`

GET `{base}/search?q=…&fq=…&fq=…&fl=…&rows=…` and return
`response.docs` (an empty array when the body has none). The generic
shape behind {@link fetchGrameneExprAttrDocs}; `/search` is used rather
than `/genes` because the latter trims docs to a fixed field set.
Origin: `Homology.js:301-312`.

```ts
function fetchGrameneSearchDocs<T = Record<string, unknown>>(base: string, params: GrameneSearchParams, opts?: GrameneFetchOptions): Promise<T[]>;
```

### `fromBrAPIAlleleMatrix`

Convert a BrAPI v2 `/allelematrix-search` response into a TBrowse
`GenotypeMatrix`. The matrix the server returns is variant-major
(`dataMatrix[v][s]`), but the zone consumes per-sample rows
(`callsByGeneId[sample] = string[]`), so the adapter transposes once
up-front — cheap relative to the cost of fetching the data and
lets the zone iterate cells in row-major order at paint time.

Origin: stale worktree `stupefied-davinci-b87dec/src/adapters/brapi.ts:38-138`,
moved verbatim apart from the strict-mode spellings noted inline
(non-null assertions on indexed reads, conditional spreads instead of
`undefined`-valued optional properties).

```ts
function fromBrAPIAlleleMatrix(raw: unknown, opts?: FromBrAPIAlleleMatrixOptions): FromBrAPIAlleleMatrixResult;
```

### `fromBrAPIGermplasm`

Convert a BrAPI v2 `/germplasm` (or `/search/germplasm`) response into
a `Record<GeneId, Germplasm>` map keyed by germplasmDbId AND
germplasmName, so a tree whose leaves carry either id can join the
map without the host having to choose up-front. The returned map is
suitable to drop straight into TBrowse's `germplasm` prop.

Standard BrAPI columns are mapped onto the matching `Germplasm`
fields; anything else on the record (institute codes, donor info,
1000 Genomes-style population labels, etc.) is preserved on the
`extras` field so a host can surface it via a custom label provider.

Origin: stale worktree `stupefied-davinci-b87dec/src/adapters/brapi.ts:162-236`, verbatim.

```ts
function fromBrAPIGermplasm(raw: unknown): Record<GeneId, Germplasm>;
```

### `fromBrAPITree`

Parse the tree block of a BrAPI allele-matrix response into a `Tree`
plus the `swappedNodeIds` that make `leafOrder(tree, { swappedNodeIds })`
reproduce the server's `leafOrder`. The Newick is parsed with
`labelsAsIds: false`, so every node id is synthetic and sample names
(which may be numeric strings) live on `geneId` only — that is what keeps
child order stable under `Object.keys` and lets `callsByGeneId[sample]`
join each leaf. Returns null when the response carries no `newick`;
`unmatched` lists leafOrder entries that name no leaf.

```ts
function fromBrAPITree(r: Pick<FromBrAPIAlleleMatrixResult, 'newick' | 'leafOrder'>, opts?: ParseNewickOptions): {
    tree: Tree;
    swappedNodeIds: NodeId[];
    unmatched: string[];
} | null;
```

### `fromBrAPIVariants`

Convert the long-form BrAPI `/variants` response of gramene-g2p — one row
per (sample, variant): `{ sample, pos, ref?, alleles, GT }`, wrapped in
`result.data` or given as a bare array — into one `VariantSite` per
position (first row per `pos` wins, in order of first appearance). `ref`
is the row's `ref`, `alt` is `alleles.slice(1)` (`alleles[0]` is REF),
and the id is synthesised as `${reference ?? ''}:${pos}` so it matches
the matrix's variantDbIds (g2p `brapi/genotyping.ts:426`). Rows without a
numeric `pos` are skipped.
Origin: stale worktree `examples/playground/main.tsx:679-700` (`loadBrapiVariants`).

```ts
function fromBrAPIVariants(raw: unknown, opts?: FromBrAPIVariantsOptions): VariantSite[];
```

### `fromEnsemblGeneStructure`

Convert one `/overlap/id/{geneId}?feature=transcript;feature=exon;feature=cds`
response into a `GeneStructure` for that gene. The caller passes the
gene's stable id so we can scope to its transcripts (the endpoint
returns features for every overlapping gene in the region).

Returns `null` when the response carries no transcripts whose
`Parent === geneId` — i.e. the gene either doesn't exist or has no
structure on file. Soft-fails on partially-malformed rows: a row
missing required numerics is skipped rather than throwing.

Pure: callers do the network fetch.

Docs: https://rest.ensembl.org/documentation/info/overlap_id

Origin: moved verbatim from `tbrowse/src/adapters/ensembl.ts:326`.

```ts
function fromEnsemblGeneStructure(json: unknown, geneId: string): GeneStructure | null;
```

### `fromEnsemblGeneTree`

Convert an Ensembl gene-tree REST response into TBrowse's normalized inputs.

Synthetic node IDs are assigned in pre-order ("n0", "n1", ...) so they are
deterministic across runs against the same response — important for URL
state round-tripping.

Pass options.alphabet explicitly if you fetched the tree with sequence=cdna
(otherwise the heuristic infers protein for any non-DNA character).

Origin: moved verbatim from `tbrowse/src/adapters/ensembl.ts:88`.

```ts
function fromEnsemblGeneTree(json: unknown, options?: FromEnsemblOptions): FromEnsemblResult;
```

### `fromEnsemblGenomeFeatures`

Convert one `/overlap/id/{geneId}?feature=regulatory;feature=motif`
response into the proximal-feature track that drives the genome
browser zone's optional annotations row.

Each regulatory element / TF binding motif becomes one
`GenomeFeature`. The endpoint also surfaces `repeat`, `simple`,
etc. when those `feature=` flags are added; the converter accepts
them all and uses the row's `feature_type_class` (regulatory) or
`feature_type` as the kind label.

Origin: moved verbatim from `tbrowse/src/adapters/ensembl.ts:479`.

```ts
function fromEnsemblGenomeFeatures(json: unknown): GenomeFeature[];
```

### `fromEnsemblProteinFeatures`

Convert an Ensembl `/overlap/translation/{ENSP}?feature=protein_feature`
response into TBrowse's ProteinDomain[] for that single protein. Pure;
the caller does the network fetch and assembles the per-GeneId dict.

Rows missing required fields (`id`, numeric `start`/`end`) are skipped
silently — Ensembl occasionally returns sparse hits that aren't useful.

Docs: https://rest.ensembl.org/documentation/info/overlap_translation

Origin: moved verbatim from `tbrowse/src/adapters/ensembl.ts:240`.

```ts
function fromEnsemblProteinFeatures(json: unknown, options?: FromEnsemblProteinFeaturesOptions): ProteinDomain[];
```

### `fromGrameneGene`

Convert a Gramene `/genes?idList=<single-id>` response into the minimal
pieces a host needs to discover the gene's tree id and bootstrap a
tbrowse view. Returns `geneTreeId: null` when the gene has no tree
assignment so the caller can decide what to do (fall back to the gene
record alone, surface an error, etc.).

Origin: moved verbatim from `tbrowse/src/adapters/gramene.ts:278`.

```ts
function fromGrameneGene(json: unknown): FromGrameneGeneResult;
```

### `fromGrameneGeneStructures`

Convert one or more Gramene `/genes` documents (each carrying
`location` + `gene_structure`) into the normalized
`GeneStructure` shape the genome browser zone consumes.

Gramene encodes exon coordinates RELATIVE to the gene's 5' end, in
transcript direction — relative position 1 is the 5'-most base of the
gene. We turn them into absolute genomic coordinates (always
`start <= end`) so the renderer doesn't have to know about Gramene's
convention. CDS bounds, given in cDNA (spliced-transcript) coords,
are walked through the exon list to mark the per-exon
`cdsStart`/`cdsEnd` ranges in genomic coords.

Skips genes that lack `location` or `gene_structure`. Pure: callers
own the network fetch.

Origin: moved verbatim from `tbrowse/src/adapters/gramene.ts:453`.

```ts
function fromGrameneGeneStructures(json: unknown): Record<GeneId, GeneStructure>;
```

### `fromGrameneGenetree`

Convert a Gramene `/genetrees?idList=...` response (an array containing
a single root node) into TBrowse's normalized inputs. Pure — host owns
the network call.

Synthetic node ids (`n0`, `n1`, ...) are assigned in preorder so they
round-trip stably through URL state.

Origin: moved verbatim from `tbrowse/src/adapters/gramene.ts:95`.

```ts
function fromGrameneGenetree(json: unknown, options?: FromGrameneGenetreeOptions): FromGrameneGenetreeResult;
```

### `fromGrameneNeighborhood`

```ts
function fromGrameneNeighborhood(json: unknown, options?: FromGrameneNeighborhoodOptions): Record<GeneId, Neighborhood>;
```

### `grameneGeneTreeRef`

Resolve a Gramene gene doc's `homology` to its tree: `gene_tree` when
present, else the first tree-set entry (an object with a string `id`).
`null` when the gene has homologues but no tree.

```ts
function grameneGeneTreeRef(homology: unknown): GrameneGeneTreeRef | null;
```

### `grameneNeighborhoodQuery`

Query parameters of the Solr graph query that returns every leaf of a
gene tree plus its ±10 flanking genes, in the order the origins set
them: `fl`, `fq='{!graph from=compara_neighbors_10 to=compara_idx_multi
maxDepth=1 cache=false}gene_tree:<treeId>'`, `rows=100000`, `start=0`.
Origin: `main.tsx:576-586`, `Homology.js:222-226`.

`cache=false` because a cached graph fq caches its seed inside its own
filterCache `computeIfAbsent`, and Solr's FastLRUCache then throws
"Recursive update" (HTTP 500) for whichever trees' keys collide.

`treeField` is the Solr field holding the tree id — `gene_tree`, or a
clade tree set such as `wheat` — and is added to `fl` when it isn't
`gene_tree`, so the neighbours' family ids come back too.

```ts
function grameneNeighborhoodQuery(treeId: string, treeField?: string): Record<string, string>;
```

### `hostPropsFrom`

Turns a snapshot into the props the `TBrowse` viewer takes: `null`
until the tree has loaded, else `{ tree, taxonomy?, nodeOfInterest?,
zoneStatus }` plus every merged host-data field. Only defined keys are
included, so the result spreads straight onto the viewer without
tripping `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`.

```ts
function hostPropsFrom<M>(s: LoaderSnapshot<M>): ({
    tree: Tree;
    taxonomy?: Taxonomy;
    nodeOfInterest?: string;
    zoneStatus: ZoneStatusMap;
} & HostDataPatch) | null;
```

### `mergeHostData`

Merges one host-data patch over another. Top-level keys are later-wins;
the opaque `hostData` channel is merged one level deep so two slots can
each contribute their own `hostData.<key>` without clobbering each other.
Keys whose value is `undefined` in `patch` are ignored. With
`warnOnOverwrite`, every top-level key (or `hostData` sub-key) that
replaces a defined value logs a `console.warn` — a dev aid for spotting
two slots that write the same field; `onOverwrite(key)` replaces the
logging (the loader uses it to report each collision only once). Always
returns a new object.

```ts
function mergeHostData(base: HostDataPatch, patch: HostDataPatch, opts?: {
    warnOnOverwrite?: boolean;
    onOverwrite?: (key: string) => void;
}): HostDataPatch;
```

### `mergeVariantSites`

Merge REF/ALT (and allele-frequency) detail from `sites` into the
matrix's variant columns. The join is by POSITION: a matrix variant with
a `position` takes the site at the same position; one without a position
matches a site by `id` only when that site also lacks a position. On a
hit, `ref`, `alt` and `alleleFrequency` are taken from the site when it
defines them and kept otherwise. Returns a new `GenotypeMatrix` (new
`variants` array) when at least one column changed, and the SAME object
when nothing matched, so a loader can tell a no-op from a change.
Origin: stale worktree `examples/playground/main.tsx:703-712`.

```ts
function mergeVariantSites(matrix: GenotypeMatrix, sites: VariantSite[]): GenotypeMatrix;
```

### `mirrorFor`

Resolve a host name to its mirror record. An unknown host is assumed to
serve `release` (default: the current release) and gets the route that
release implies (`'species'` for >= 112, `'bare'` below 110, either in
between — we pick `'species'`), so a new archive works before the table
is updated.

```ts
function mirrorFor(host: string, release?: number): EnsemblMirror;
```

### `staticSource`

Wraps a function of the context into a `TreeDataSource` whose
`loadRoot` awaits `rootOf(ctx)` (sync or async). Handy for in-memory
trees, fixtures and tests; the optional `slots` are attached unchanged.

```ts
function staticSource<Ctx, M>(rootOf: (ctx: Ctx) => RootResult<M> | Promise<RootResult<M>>, slots?: readonly DataSlot<any, Ctx, M>[]): TreeDataSource<Ctx, M>;
```

### `zoneStatusOf`

Derives per-zone status from per-slot status through the host's
zone id → slot ids map. A zone is `'loading'` when any mapped slot is
loading, else `'error'` when any mapped slot errored, else `'ready'`
when the mapped slots that have started are all ready. Idle (not yet
started: lazy, disabled) and undeclared slot ids do not participate, so
a zone whose mapped slots are all idle — and a zone with no mapped
slots — is absent from the result (`undefined`).

```ts
function zoneStatusOf(slots: Record<string, SlotState>, zoneSlots: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>): ZoneStatusMap;
```

## Constants

### `brapiAlleleMatrixSource`

`TreeDataSource` for a BrAPI `/allelematrix-search` window. The root
fetches the matrix and takes the server's tree when the response has one
(`fromBrAPITree`: synthetic node ids, sample names on `geneId`, swaps that
reproduce `leafOrder`); otherwise `ctx.treeFallback` decides: `'upgma'`
(default) clusters the matrix locally with the same metric gramene-g2p
uses, `'star'` hangs every sample off one root, `'none'` throws
`'BrAPI: response has no tree'`. Leaves are keyed so
`matrix.callsByGeneId[leaf.geneId]` joins; `root.data` is `{}` because
the genotype zone reads the matrix from `meta`. Slots: `germplasm`
(eager → `{ germplasm }`, filtered to the tree's samples) and `variants`
(eager; host data `{}`, `patchMeta` merges the REF/ALT sites into
`meta.matrix`).

```ts
const brapiAlleleMatrixSource: TreeDataSource<BrapiCtx, BrapiMeta>;
```

### `ENSEMBL_DEFAULT_DOMAIN_SOURCES`

Protein-feature sources kept by default (`type` field of each row).

```ts
const ENSEMBL_DEFAULT_DOMAIN_SOURCES: readonly string[];
```

### `ENSEMBL_DEFAULT_MIRROR`

The current (load-sensitive) endpoint; the default when a host names none.

```ts
const ENSEMBL_DEFAULT_MIRROR = "rest.ensembl.org";
```

### `ENSEMBL_MIRRORS`

Known Ensembl REST hosts, newest release first. Release 106 (apr2022) is
deliberately absent: that host accepts TCP connections but never
responds. Expect one maintenance edit per Ensembl release.

```ts
const ENSEMBL_MIRRORS: readonly EnsemblMirror[];
```

### `ensemblGeneTreeSource`

The Ensembl gene-tree data source: the root is the gene tree containing
`ctx.geneId` ({@link fetchEnsemblGeneTree}: tree, taxonomy, aligned MSA,
gene metadata), pivoted on that gene. Two lazy slots fan out to the
same mirror on demand: `proteinDomains` ({@link fetchEnsemblProteinDomains};
errors with 'No protein ids on this tree' when the tree carried no
translation ids and with `All N domain requests failed (…)` when nothing
came back, otherwise ready with per-gene `itemErrors`) and `overlap`
({@link fetchEnsemblOverlap}; per-leaf failures are delivered as
`geneStructureErrors` data, never as a slot error). Origin: the
playground's Ensembl path, `examples/playground/main.tsx:88-137, 458-655`.

```ts
const ensemblGeneTreeSource: TreeDataSource<EnsemblCtx, EnsemblMeta>;
```

### `fileTreeSource`

The file data source: the root is `parseTreeSource(ctx.file, …)` — the
format is sniffed from the content (then from the filename extension),
the PhyloXML parser takes `ctx.parseDocument` / `ctx.DOMParser` by
injection, and a PhyloXML taxonomy is passed through. Parse errors
reject the root load; soft warnings land in `meta.warnings`. No slots:
tables that accompany a tree are parsed by the host (`parseTableFile`).

```ts
const fileTreeSource: TreeDataSource<FileTreeCtx, FileTreeMeta>;
```

### `GRAMENE_DEFAULT_BASE`

The Gramene REST base the playground uses (`main.tsx:167`).

```ts
const GRAMENE_DEFAULT_BASE = "https://data.gramene.org/v69";
```

### `GRAMENE_DEFAULT_TREE_FIELD`

Where a gene's tree id lives, in the gene doc's `homology` and in Solr,
for the main Compara trees. Genomes in a clade-specific tree set (v70:
wheat, oat) carry it under the set's name instead —
`homology.wheat = { id: 'EplWheatGT_…' }`, Solr field `wheat` — and the
tree doc's root names the set in `tree_set`.

```ts
const GRAMENE_DEFAULT_TREE_FIELD = "gene_tree";
```

### `GRAMENE_GENE_STRUCTURE_FL`

The narrow field list the playground requests for gene structures (`main.tsx:618`).

```ts
const GRAMENE_GENE_STRUCTURE_FL = "_id,name,location,gene_structure,canonical_transcript";
```

### `grameneGeneTreeSource`

The Gramene gene-tree data source. Root: when `ctx.treeId` is absent,
`GET /genes?idList=<geneId>` resolves the tree id (error when the gene
has none); then the tree comes from `ctx.rawGenetree` when given (so a
host that already holds the `/genetrees` doc makes no request) or from
`GET /genetrees?idList=<treeId>`. The root carries the MSA, gene
metadata, per-leaf protein domains and exon junctions that the genetree
response already contains, pivoted on `ctx.geneId`. Two eager slots
follow: `neighborhood` (one Solr graph query, {@link fetchGrameneNeighborhood})
and `geneStructures` (chunked `/genes`, {@link fetchGrameneGeneStructures};
ready with per-gene `itemErrors` on partial failure, an error only when
every chunk failed). Origin: `main.tsx:645-705`, `Homology.js:217-290`.

```ts
const grameneGeneTreeSource: TreeDataSource<GrameneCtx, GrameneMeta>;
```

## Interfaces

### `BrapiCtx`

What `brapiAlleleMatrixSource.loadRoot` needs.

```ts
interface BrapiCtx {
    /** Full `/allelematrix-search` URL (relative URLs are fine), including `tree=upgma` when the server supports it. */
    matrixUrl: string;
    /** BrAPI base for `/germplasm`; default `brapiBaseOf(matrixUrl)`. */
    base?: string;
    /** Overrides the matrix's synthesised region label. */
    regionLabel?: string;
    /** What to do when the response carries no tree (default `'upgma'`). */
    treeFallback?: 'upgma' | 'star' | 'none';
    /** Set false to skip the `germplasm` slot. */
    germplasm?: boolean;
    /** Set false to skip the `variants` slot. */
    variants?: boolean;
}
```

### `BrapiFetchOptions`

Transport options shared by every fetch helper here.

```ts
interface BrapiFetchOptions {
    fetch?: FetchLike;
    signal?: AbortSignal;
}
```

### `BrapiMeta`

`RootResult.meta` of `brapiAlleleMatrixSource`.

```ts
interface BrapiMeta {
    /** The genotype matrix; the `variants` slot replaces it with a REF/ALT-enriched copy. */
    matrix: GenotypeMatrix;
    /** callSetDbIds in server order (= leaf geneIds). */
    sampleIds: string[];
    variantSetDbId?: string;
    /** Swaps that make the viewer reproduce the server's `leafOrder`. */
    swappedNodeIds: NodeId[];
    treeMethod?: string;
    treeMetric?: string;
}
```

### `BrapiPage`

One page of a paged BrAPI list response (`result.data` + `metadata.pagination`).

```ts
interface BrapiPage<T> {
    data: T[];
    currentPage: number;
    totalPages: number;
    totalCount: number;
}
```

### `BrapiVariantSetTree`

A precomputed variant-set tree, as gramene-g2p serves it.

```ts
interface BrapiVariantSetTree {
    newick: string;
    leafOrder: string[];
    method?: string;
    metric?: string;
}
```

### `DataSlot`

```ts
interface DataSlot<T, Ctx = unknown, M = Record<string, unknown>> {
    id: string;
    /** Default 'eager' = runs right after the root. */
    mode?: 'eager' | 'lazy';
    enabled?: (ctx: Ctx, root: RootResult<M>) => boolean;
    run(sc: SlotContext<Ctx, M>): Promise<T>;
    toHostData(value: T, root: RootResult<M>): HostDataPatch;
    /** Optional: expose per-item failures (fanOut errors) so the loader records them without failing the slot. */
    itemErrorsOf?(value: T): Record<string, string> | null;
    /** Optional: turn a resolved value into a slot error (e.g. "all N requests failed"); returning null keeps 'ready'. */
    failWhen?(value: T, itemErrors: Record<string, string> | null): string | null;
    /** Optional: update root metadata (e.g. merge variant sites into meta.matrix). Must return a NEW object when anything changed; the loader then replaces snapshot.root. */
    patchMeta?(value: T, meta: M, root: RootResult<M>): M;
}
```

### `EnsemblCtx`

Context for {@link ensemblGeneTreeSource}.

```ts
interface EnsemblCtx {
    /** Member gene id, e.g. `ENSG00000139618`. */
    geneId: string;
    /** REST host; default `ENSEMBL_DEFAULT_MIRROR`. */
    host?: string;
    /** Species segment for the `'species'` route; default `homo_sapiens`. */
    species?: string;
    /** Protein-feature sources for the `proteinDomains` slot; default Pfam + Smart. */
    domainSources?: readonly string[];
}
```

### `EnsemblGeneTreeUrlOptions`

```ts
interface EnsemblGeneTreeUrlOptions {
    /** REST host; default `ENSEMBL_DEFAULT_MIRROR`. */
    host?: string;
    /** Species segment for the >= 112 route; default `homo_sapiens`. */
    species?: string;
    /** `sequence=` query value; default `'protein'`. */
    sequence?: 'protein' | 'cdna' | 'none';
    /** `aligned=1` (default true) returns the aligned member sequences. */
    aligned?: boolean;
}
```

### `EnsemblMeta`

Root metadata of {@link ensemblGeneTreeSource}.

```ts
interface EnsemblMeta {
    /** Gene id → translation (ENSP) accession, as the gene-tree response carried it. */
    proteinIdByGeneId: Record<GeneId, string>;
    /** The mirror the tree was loaded from; slots fan out to the same host. */
    mirror: EnsemblMirror;
}
```

### `EnsemblMirror`

One Ensembl REST host. Archive hosts pin a single release and run on
infrastructure separate from the main `rest.ensembl.org` endpoint, which
intermittently sheds load with 5xx when traffic spikes; picking an
archive trades currency for consistency.

`route` is not cosmetic: the gene-tree member endpoint changed shape
mid-history. Releases <= 109 answer only `/genetree/member/id/{gene}`;
releases >= 112 answer only `/genetree/member/id/{species}/{gene}`; 110
and 111 accept both. Sending the wrong form gets a 404.

```ts
interface EnsemblMirror {
    /** Hostname, and the stable id a host persists in its URL state. */
    host: string;
    /** Ensembl release served by this host. */
    release: number;
    /** Gene-tree member route shape this release understands. */
    route: 'bare' | 'species';
}
```

### `EnsemblOverlapResult`

What {@link fetchEnsemblOverlap} resolves to: three `HostData`-shaped maps.

```ts
interface EnsemblOverlapResult {
    geneStructures: Record<GeneId, GeneStructure>;
    genomeFeatures: Record<GeneId, GenomeFeature[]>;
    /** Per-gene failures (HTTP status, parse error, or no gene model in the response). */
    geneStructureErrors: Record<GeneId, string>;
}
```

```ts
    /** Species segment for the `'species'` route; default `homo_sapiens`. */

    signal?: AbortSignal;
```
```ts
}
```

### `FileTreeMeta`

Root metadata of {@link fileTreeSource}.

### `FromBrAPIAlleleMatrixOptions`

```ts

    /** Optional human-readable region label for the zone header. Falls back
     *  to a label assembled from the response's `referenceName` / variant
     *  span when not supplied. */
    regionLabel?: string;

```

### `FromBrAPIAlleleMatrixResult`

Result of converting a BrAPI v2 `/allelematrix-search` response. The
genotype matrix is normalised onto TBrowse's `GenotypeMatrix` shape
(per-leaf row keyed by `geneId`, parallel to a list of variants), and
the response's optional Newick tree string is surfaced verbatim so
the host can parse it with whatever Newick parser it already owns —
the adapter intentionally stays out of tree parsing to avoid
doubling up with the host's existing tree pipeline.

```ts
interface FromBrAPIAlleleMatrixResult {
    /** Per-sample genotype calls + per-variant column metadata. */
    matrix: GenotypeMatrix;
    /** callSetDbIds in the order returned by the server. Useful when the
     *  host wants to render the matrix without a tree. */
    sampleIds: string[];
    /** First variantSetDbId on the response (most BrAPI servers return one). */
    variantSetDbId?: string;
    /** Optional Newick tree string. BrAPI servers return this only when
     *  the request includes a `tree=…` parameter. */
    newick?: string;
    /** Tree method label from the response (e.g. `"upgma"`). */
    treeMethod?: string;
    /** Tree distance metric label from the response. */
    treeMetric?: string;
    /** Server-supplied display order of leaves, when present. */
    leafOrder?: string[];
}
```

### `FromBrAPIVariantsOptions`

```ts
interface FromBrAPIVariantsOptions {
    /** Reference (chromosome) name the rows belong to; the long-form rows
     *  carry only `pos`, so this is what makes the synthesised id match the
     *  matrix's `<reference>:<pos>` variantDbIds. */
    reference?: string;
}
```

### `FromEnsemblOptions`

```ts
interface FromEnsemblOptions {
    /**
     * Override the MSA alphabet. When omitted, alphabet is sniffed from the
     * sequence contents (DNA if every character matches /[ACGTN-]/i,
     * protein otherwise). Pass explicitly when you fetched cdna or are
     * working with non-standard residue characters.
     */
    alphabet?: MSA['alphabet'];
}
```

### `FromEnsemblProteinFeaturesOptions`

```ts
interface FromEnsemblProteinFeaturesOptions {
    /**
     * Restrict to specific feature sources (Ensembl's `type` field —
     * case-sensitive: `"Pfam"`, `"Smart"`, `"SuperFamily"`, `"PANTHER"`,
     * `"Gene3D"`, `"Prints"`, `"PIRSF"`, `"Tmhmm"`, `"Signalp"`, ...).
     * Pass `undefined` or an empty list to keep every source.
     */
    sources?: ReadonlyArray<string>;
}
```

### `FromEnsemblResult`

```ts
interface FromEnsemblResult {
    tree: Tree;
    taxonomy: Taxonomy;
    msa?: MSA;
    geneMetadata: GeneMetadata;
    /**
     * GeneId → translation (ENSP) accession, when the gene-tree response
     * carried it. Hosts use this to fan out to
     * `/overlap/translation/{ENSP}?feature=protein_feature` and feed the
     * results into `fromEnsemblProteinFeatures`. Missing entries simply
     * mean we couldn't resolve a protein id for that leaf — skip those.
     */
    proteinIdByGeneId: Record<GeneId, string>;
}
```

### `FromGrameneGeneResult`

```ts
interface FromGrameneGeneResult {
    geneId: GeneId;
    /** The gene's tree id, from `gene_tree` or its clade tree set; `null` when it has none. */
    geneTreeId: string | null;
    /** Solr field / tree set holding {@link geneTreeId}; `null` with it. */
    geneTreeField: string | null;
    taxonomyId: number | null;
    systemName: string | null;
    description: string | null;
}
```

### `FromGrameneGenetreeOptions`

```ts
interface FromGrameneGenetreeOptions {
    /**
     * Override the MSA alphabet. Defaults to 'protein' (Gramene gene-tree
     * leaves carry protein sequences).
     */
    alphabet?: MSA['alphabet'];
}
```

### `FromGrameneGenetreeResult`

```ts
interface FromGrameneGenetreeResult {
    tree: Tree;
    taxonomy: Taxonomy;
    msa?: MSA;
    geneMetadata: GeneMetadata;
    /** Per-leaf protein-domain hits, ready to drop into HostData.proteinDomains. */
    proteinDomains: Record<GeneId, ProteinDomain[]>;
    /** Per-leaf splice-junction positions (1-based unaligned residue),
     *  ready to drop into HostData.exonJunctions. */
    exonJunctions: Record<GeneId, number[]>;
    /** GeneId → translation accession (for parity with the Ensembl adapter). */
    proteinIdByGeneId: Record<GeneId, string>;
    /**
     * The root's `tree_set` — `'gene_tree'` for the main Compara trees, the
     * clade set (`'wheat'`, `'oat'`, …) otherwise — which is also the Solr
     * field holding the tree id. {@link GRAMENE_DEFAULT_TREE_FIELD} when the
     * doc predates tree sets (v69 and earlier).
     */
    treeField: string;
}
```

### `FromGrameneNeighborhoodOptions`

Convert a Gramene `/search` graph-query response into per-gene
neighbourhood windows.

The response carries every gene within ±10 of any leaf in the source
tree (3601 docs for a moderately-sized tree). We index by
`(system_name, region) → sorted-by-gene_idx`, then for every gene we
emit a `Neighborhood` whose `upstream`/`downstream` arrays are at
most 10 genes long, sliced from that sorted index.

Pure: callers do the network fetch, hand us the JSON.

Origin: moved verbatim from `tbrowse/src/adapters/gramene.ts:338`.

```ts
interface FromGrameneNeighborhoodOptions {
    /**
     * Field holding each gene's family accession (`NeighborhoodGene.geneTree`);
     * default {@link GRAMENE_DEFAULT_TREE_FIELD}. For a clade tree pass its set
     * (`'wheat'`), so neighbours are coloured by the same family ids as the tree.
     */
    treeField?: string;
}
```

### `GrameneCtx`

Context for {@link grameneGeneTreeSource}.

```ts
interface GrameneCtx {
    /** REST base; default {@link GRAMENE_DEFAULT_BASE}. */
    base?: string;
    /** Gene whose tree to load (resolved through `/genes` unless `treeId` is given); also the node of interest. */
    geneId?: string;
    /** Tree id, when already known: skips the `/genes` lookup. */
    treeId?: string;
    /**
     * Solr field / tree set holding `treeId`. Rarely needed: the source takes
     * it from the tree doc's `tree_set`, or from the gene lookup.
     */
    treeField?: string;
    /**
     * An already-fetched `/genetrees` response (the bare root doc or the
     * one-element array), normalised with `Array.isArray(x) ? x : [x]`.
     * Together with `treeId` the root load makes no request at all.
     */
    rawGenetree?: unknown;
    /** Set `false` to skip the `neighborhood` slot. */
    neighborhood?: boolean;
    /** Set `false` to skip the `geneStructures` slot. */
    geneStructures?: boolean;
    /** Gene ids per `/genes` request for the `geneStructures` slot; default 200 (gramene-search passes 50). */
    geneStructureChunkSize?: number;
    /** `fl` for the `geneStructures` slot; default the narrow list, `null` omits it. */
    geneStructureFl?: string | null;
}
```

### `GrameneFetchOptions`

Transport options shared by every fetch helper here.

```ts
interface GrameneFetchOptions {
    fetch?: FetchLike;
    signal?: AbortSignal;
}
```

### `GrameneGeneTreeRef`

A gene's tree: its id and the field (tree set) that holds it.

```ts
interface GrameneGeneTreeRef {
    id: string;
    field: string;
}
```

### `GrameneMeta`

Root metadata of {@link grameneGeneTreeSource}.

```ts
interface GrameneMeta {
    treeId: string;
    /** Solr field holding `treeId` (`gene_tree`, or a clade set like `wheat`); scopes the tree's `/search` queries. */
    treeField: string;
    /** The `/genes` lookup result, when the root had to resolve `geneId` to a tree. */
    gene?: FromGrameneGeneResult;
    /** Gene id → translation accession (parity with the Ensembl source). */
    proteinIdByGeneId: Record<GeneId, string>;
}
```

### `GrameneSearchParams`

Parameters of {@link fetchGrameneSearchDocs}.

```ts
interface GrameneSearchParams {
    /** Solr `q`; default `'*:*'`. */
    q?: string;
    /** Solr `fq` filters, sent as repeated `fq=` parameters. */
    fq: readonly string[];
    /** Solr `fl` field list (globs allowed). */
    fl: string;
    /** Solr `rows`; omitted when undefined (the server default applies). */
    rows?: number;
}
```

### `GrameneTreeQueryOptions`

Options for the tree-scoped `/search` helpers.

```ts
interface GrameneTreeQueryOptions extends GrameneFetchOptions {
    /** Solr field holding the tree id; default `gene_tree` (a clade set such as `wheat` otherwise). */
    treeField?: string;
}
```

### `Loader`

```ts
interface Loader<Ctx = unknown, M = Record<string, unknown>> {
    readonly source: TreeDataSource<Ctx, M>;
    /** Same reference until something changes (useSyncExternalStore-safe). */
    getSnapshot(): LoaderSnapshot<M>;
    subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void;
    /** Aborts the previous generation; loads the root, then the enabled eager slots. */
    start(ctx: Ctx): Promise<LoaderSnapshot<M>>;
    /** Lazy slots, or retry an errored one. */
    load(slotId: string): Promise<void>;
    abort(): void;
    dispose(): void;
}
```

### `LoaderOptions`

```ts
interface LoaderOptions {
    fetch?: FetchLike;
    retry?: RetryOptions;
    concurrency?: number;
    /** Host zone id → slot ids that feed it. */
    zoneSlots?: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>;
    /** Dev aid: warn when two slots write the same top-level key. */
    warnOnOverwrite?: boolean;
}
```

### `LoaderSnapshot`

```ts
interface LoaderSnapshot<M = Record<string, unknown>> {
    /** Status of the root load. */
    status: SlotStatus;
    error: string | null;
    tree: Tree | null;
    /** Replaced (new reference) when a slot's `patchMeta` returns a new meta. */
    root: RootResult<M> | null;
    /** `root.data` + `toHostData()` of every ready slot, merged in slot order. */
    data: HostDataPatch;
    slots: Record<string, SlotState>;
    /** `zoneStatusOf(slots, options.zoneSlots)`. */
    zoneStatus: ZoneStatusMap;
    /** `computePivotState(tree, root.nodeOfInterest)`. */
    pivot: PivotState | null;
    /** Bumps on every `start()`; stale async results are dropped. */
    generation: number;
}
```

### `RootContext`

```ts
interface RootContext<Ctx> {
    ctx: Ctx;
    /** Already retry-wrapped. */
    fetch: FetchLike;
    signal: AbortSignal;
}
```

### `RootResult`

What a source's root load yields: the tree plus whatever arrived with it. `M` = source-specific metadata, typed.

```ts
interface RootResult<M = Record<string, unknown>> {
    tree: Tree;
    taxonomy?: Taxonomy;
    /** Gene id or node id; fed to `computePivotState`. */
    nodeOfInterest?: string;
    /** msa, geneMetadata, proteinDomains, … that came with the tree. */
    data?: HostDataPatch;
    /** e.g. `{ proteinIdByGeneId }`, `{ treeId }`, `{ matrix, swappedNodeIds }`. */
    meta: M;
}
```

### `SlotContext`

```ts
interface SlotContext<Ctx, M> extends RootContext<Ctx> {
    tree: Tree;
    root: RootResult<M>;
    onProgress: (p: FanOutProgress) => void;
    /** `LoaderOptions.concurrency`, for slots that fan out per leaf. */
    concurrency?: number;
}
```

### `SlotState`

```ts
interface SlotState<T = unknown> {
    status: SlotStatus;
    value: T | undefined;
    error: string | null;
    /** Live during fan-outs. */
    progress: FanOutProgress | null;
    /** Per-leaf failures: the slot is 'ready' with partial data. */
    itemErrors: Record<string, string> | null;
}
```

### `TreeDataSource`

```ts
interface TreeDataSource<Ctx = unknown, M = Record<string, unknown>> {
    id: string;
    label?: string;
    loadRoot(rc: RootContext<Ctx>): Promise<RootResult<M>>;
    slots: readonly DataSlot<any, Ctx, M>[];
}
```

## Type aliases

### `SlotStatus`

The data-source contract: a `TreeDataSource` loads a root (the tree and
whatever arrived with it) and declares `DataSlot`s — independently
fetched per-leaf data that becomes `HostData` fields. A `Loader` runs a
source and exposes a snapshot (tree, merged host data, per-slot status,
per-zone status) that a React host can subscribe to with
`useSyncExternalStore`, or a script can simply `await`.

Slots carry NO zone ids: zone ids are host-assigned (`createGenomeZone({ id })`,
`createGenotypeMatrixZone({ id })`), so the host maps zone id → slot ids
through `LoaderOptions.zoneSlots`.

```ts
type SlotStatus = 'idle' | 'loading' | 'ready' | 'error';
```
